title: Terms of Acceptance and Commencement of a Lease of Safe Deposit Boxes
content:
Safe Deposit Boxes are let on a lease that begins when an offered box is accepted. When a box of the size reserved becomes free, it is offered to the waitlisted customer next in priority. These terms govern the hold placed on that offer and what follows the customer's acceptance of it.

## The hold on an offered box

An offered box is held for the customer only within 10 calendar days after the offer.

Calendar days are counted with the day after the offer date as day 1. The customer may accept while the current date is on or before the offer date plus 10 days, after which the reservation lapses. The offer date is the date recorded against that rental when the offer was made, and it is that record, read for the rental being accepted, that fixes the day the count runs from.

## Commencement

On acceptance the lease is signed by the lessee, two keys are issued, the key deposit is charged as a service charge on the rental, and the first year's rent is charged on the lease start date.

## Contents

The bank does not insure the contents of a box of any size. A lessee asking about insuring the contents is referred to the lessee's own insurer.

## The hold period at its boundary

Suppose, on hypothetical dates, that the offer is made on 4 March. The day after the offer date, 5 March, is day 1, and the tenth day is therefore 14 March.

| Date the customer accepts | Within the hold | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13 March, hypothetically | yes, day 9 | the acceptance stands |
| 14 March, hypothetically | yes, day 10, the last day of the hold | the acceptance stands |
| 15 March, hypothetically | no, the hold has run out | the reservation has lapsed |

The boundary is inclusive: an acceptance on the tenth day itself is within the hold. It is the offer date, not the reservation date, that the 10 days run from, so a customer who reserved months earlier gets the same 10 days as one who reserved the week before.
